stages.handoff:
**Diagnosis:** `:buffer` is still the registered command in [commands.py](/app/qutebrowser/browser/commands.py:919). Registration derives the user-visible name from the function name, so command completion and generated help continue to expose `buffer`. The implementation already supports count precedence, numeric and `win_id/index` references, title and URL matching, and foregrounding the selected window.

A fix should register `tab-select`, update its completion and matching calls to `tabs`, and change `tab-take` to use `other_tabs` in [miscmodels.py](/app/qutebrowser/completion/models/miscmodels.py:165). It should also update the `gt` binding in [configdata.yml](/app/qutebrowser/config/configdata.yml:3318), regenerate the checked-in [command help](/app/doc/help/commands.asciidoc:232) and [settings help](/app/doc/help/settings.asciidoc:653), and revise existing tests that invoke `:buffer`.

**Uncertainty:** I inspected the code and tests but did not run tests. I made no project source or test edits because this specialist assignment explicitly limits me to fault localization; the diagnosis is recorded in `.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md`.

Replaced the registered `:buffer` command with `:tab-select` and renamed its completion providers to `tabs` and `other_tabs`. Updated the `gt` binding, regenerated command and settings help, and revised the existing tests. The tab selection logic retains index and title/URL matching, count precedence, and cross-window activation.

The completion suite reported **73 passed**, and a registry check confirmed `tab-select` is present while `buffer` is absent. The test process then exited with an X11 teardown error. End-to-end scenarios could not start because QtWebKit is unavailable in this environment.

VERDICT: FIX

**Code review:** I found no defect in the applied patch. `tab-select` is registered, uses the renamed tab completion providers, and appears in current help and the default binding. `git diff --check` passed. I made no project code changes.

**TEST_ENVIRONMENT_PROBLEM:** The initial end-to-end run failed before command execution because its default QtWebKit backend is unavailable. It was interrupted after repeated startup failures. Using the installed QtWebEngine backend resolved that startup problem. One existing cross-window scenario remains skipped, so its behavior was not verified.

Relevant test commands and results:

- `xvfb-run -a python3 -m pytest -p no:xvfb -q tests/unit/completion/test_models.py tests/unit/api/test_cmdutils.py tests/unit/commands/test_runners.py` — **294 passed, 1 skipped**.
- `xvfb-run -a env QUTE_BDD_WEBENGINE=true QTWEBENGINE_DISABLE_SANDBOX=1 python3 -m pytest -p no:xvfb -q --reruns 0 tests/end2end/features/test_tabs_bdd.py tests/end2end/features/test_completion_bdd.py -k 'tabselect or using_command_completion or using_help_completion or deleting_an_open_tab_via_the_completion or go_to_tab_after_moving_a_tab'` — **17 passed, 1 skipped**.
- The same end-to-end selection without the QtWebEngine environment variables produced **13 startup failures and 1 skip** before I interrupted it.

Use the QtWebEngine command above for this environment. Stabilize and enable the skipped cross-window scenario to verify that requirement. The required [checkpoint](/app/.codex-role-output/checkpoint.md) records the full review and test history.
